title: Condition (B) for a flat locally constant constructible sheaf
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $\Lambda=\mathbf F_\ell$, let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian $\Lambda$-algebra. Work with module sheaves and their ordinary derived categories on the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. Constructible means locally constant with finitely generated stalks on a finite locally closed stratification [def-constructible-stratification], [def-weil-pbc-locally-constant-finite-type-modules], [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. A Galois partition $\mathcal P$ is a finite locally closed stratification of $X$ by connected reduced subschemes $S_i$, with a connected finite etale Galois covering $V_i\to S_i$ for each stratum. Here Galois means that a finite group acts on the cover and acts simply transitively on every geometric fibre. Let $\mathcal W_{\mathcal P}(A)$ be the class of sheaves whose restriction to each $S_i$ is a filtered colimit of sheaves obtained by finite successive extensions of locally constant $A$-module sheaves which become constant on $V_i$. No finite-generation condition is imposed in $\mathcal W_{\mathcal P}(A)$. Write $D^b_{\mathcal P}(X,A)$ for bounded complexes whose cohomology sheaves belong to this class. Let $F$ be a locally constant constructible flat sheaf of $A_X$-modules, where flat means that tensoring module sheaves with $F$ is exact. For every Galois partition $\mathcal P$, there is a Galois partition $\mathcal P\prime$ such that for every $u\le v$ and $N\in D^b_{\mathcal P}(X,A)\cap D^{[u,v]}$, one has $R\mathcal Hom_A(F,N)\in D^b_{\mathcal P\prime}(X,A)\cap D^{[u,v]}$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. If $N$ is constructible, then this internal Hom is constructible. The partition may be chosen to refine $\mathcal P$; no dualizing hypothesis is required. Locally constant is meant etale-locally, as in [def-weil-pbc-locally-constant-finite-type-modules]: $F$ is not assumed to become constant on a finite etale cover of a connected component of $X$, since with infinite finitely generated stalks such a cover need not exist.

source.place: Expose XVII, Lemma 7.6.11 and proof of Proposition 7.6.9, p. 314

proof.text: Tensoring with $F$ is an exact functor by hypothesis. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] to any complex $K$ gives $H^q(F\otimes_A K)=F\otimes_A H^q(K)$. Thus $F[0]$ is K-flat by the definition in [def-kun-derived-tensor], and $F[0]\otimes_A^L G[0]=(F\otimes_A G)[0]$ for every module sheaf $G$. In particular $F[0]$ is constructible of Tor amplitude $[0,0]$. Apply [lem-per-noetherian-ctf-flat-model] with $a=b=0$. Its representative has just one term $E^0$, so the representing quasi-isomorphism gives $E^0\cong F$. Its additional assertion supplies a Galois partition $\mathcal Q=(W_i\to T_i)$ on whose covers $F$ is constant with finite projective $A$-module values. Transfer these isomorphisms from $E^0$ to $F$.

source.place: Lemma 7.6.11, first sentence of proof; the stratified replacement of its trivializing cover uses the flat-model statement

proof.text: The assumed local constancy of $F$ provides etale trivializations $F|_U\cong\underline M_U$, with $M$ finitely generated, by [def-weil-pbc-locally-constant-finite-type-modules]. On each nonempty such $U$ choose a geometric point. Its image belongs to one $T_i$, and the geometric point lifts to $W_i\to T_i$ after extending the separably closed field if necessary. The fibre of $F$ there is the finite projective module supplied by Step 1, and is also $M$. These fibre identifications follow from the pointed-neighbourhood definition [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], or equivalently by composing geometric inverse images; constant coefficients and their module pullbacks are identified by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Hence $M$ is finite projective. Discard empty covering members. We have proved that $F$ is etale-locally a direct summand of a finite free $A_X$-module, without asserting a global finite etale trivialization.

source.place: Lemma 7.6.11, local finite-projective calculation, with the distinction in Exercise 7.2.7 retained

proof.text: Put $T(G)=\mathcal Hom_A(F,G)$ and $D=T(A_X)$, using [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. On a trivializing $U$, choose $i:M\to A^r$, $p:A^r\to M$ with $pi=1$ and put $e=ip$. Precomposition identifies $T(G)|_U$ with $\operatorname{im}(e^*:(G|_U)^r\to(G|_U)^r)$. Indeed the two maps are $h\mapsto hp$ and $f\mapsto fi$, and their composite on $T(G)|_U$ is the identity. This is a natural retract of the finite-sum functor. Given an exact sequence, apply its idempotent to a local lift to see that the sequence of image summands is exact. Restriction to $U$ is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]; the cover detects vanishing of its homology sheaves by [lem-sfb-sheaf-cover-local-isomorphism]. Therefore $T$ is exact. By [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-locally-constant], sections of constant additive sheaves are locally constant functions. The constant matrix $e^*$ acts pointwise; functions into its image locally lift to constant elements, so its sheaf image is the constant sheaf of its module image. On the same charts, $D=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,A)}$ is a retract of $A_U^r$, hence is flat and locally constant of finite type. The canonical maps $D\otimes_A G\to T(G)$ are isomorphisms on these charts by [lem-pc-finite-projective-internal-hom-evaluation], and hence globally by the cover criterion. This identifies $T$ with tensoring by the flat sheaf $D$.

source.place: Lemma 7.6.11, exact local Hom calculation; finite-projective evaluation as in Stacks 08DQ

proof.text: For any scheme morphism $g:Y\to X$, the inverse images of the charts in Step 2 cover $Y$. Exactness and additivity in [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] carry the image of the idempotent $e^*$ on $G^r$ to its image on $(g^*G)^r$. The latter is exactly $\mathcal Hom_A(g^*F,g^*G)$, by the same retraction maps. The canonical Hom pullback comparison is therefore an isomorphism: locally it is the identity on that image. In particular $g^*D=\mathcal Hom_A(g^*F,A_Y)$. If $g$ is the composite $W_i\to T_i\to X$ from Step 1, $g^*F=\underline{M_i}$ with $M_i$ finite projective, so $g^*D=\underline{\operatorname{Hom}_A(M_i,A)}$. The last identification is the same constant finite-summand calculation as in Step 3. Consequently $D\in\mathcal W_{\mathcal Q}(A)$, with a filtration of length one on each stratum.

source.place: Lemma 7.6.11, trivializing cover argument after restriction to the chosen strata

proof.text:
Represent $N$ by a complex $K$ and take a K-injective resolution $K\to I$. By [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], $R\mathcal Hom_A(F,N)$ is represented by the termwise complex $T(I)$, since $F$ is in degree zero. Exactness of $T$ and [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] show that $T(K)\to T(I)$ is a quasi-isomorphism and that, for every $q$,
$$H^qR\mathcal Hom_A(F,N)\cong T(H^qN)\cong D\otimes_A H^qN.$$
This works for arbitrary stalk sizes and any representative $K$: there is no global-section exactness assertion and no claim that $F$ is a projective object of the sheaf category.

source.place: Lemma 7.6.11, first assertion about cohomological degrees; exact-functor cohomology is Stacks 010N

proof.text: Given $\mathcal P$, apply [lem-per-galois-partition-exact-refinement] to $\mathcal P$ and the single partition $\mathcal Q$ fixed in Step 1. Obtain a common Galois refinement $\mathcal R$ with $\mathcal W_{\mathcal P}(A),\mathcal W_{\mathcal Q}(A)\subseteq\mathcal W_{\mathcal R}(A)$. For every admissible $N$, Step 4 places $D$ in $\mathcal W_{\mathcal R}(A)$ and the hypothesis places each $H^qN$ there. By [lem-per-galois-partition-tensor-closure], $D\otimes_A H^qN$ also belongs to $\mathcal W_{\mathcal R}(A)$. Notice that only the stated inclusions of weakly constructible classes are used: we do not infer from them that $F$ becomes constant on the individual covers of $\mathcal R$.

source.place: Lemma 7.6.11, final common-refinement argument; Definitions 7.3.2-7.3.3 and Exercise 7.3.8

proof.text: Take $\mathcal P\prime=\mathcal R$. By the cohomology formula of Step 5, all cohomology sheaves of $R\mathcal Hom_A(F,N)$ vanish outside $[u,v]$ and belong to $\mathcal W_{\mathcal R}(A)$ inside that interval. Thus it lies in $D^b_{\mathcal P\prime}(X,A)\cap D^{[u,v]}$. The partition was chosen from $F$ and $\mathcal P$ alone, independently of $u,v,N$, and refines $\mathcal P$. If $X$ is empty all the sheaves vanish and the empty partition works. None of the steps uses a dualizing complex.

source.place: Lemma 7.6.11, bound c=0 and final sentence

proof.text: Suppose $N$ is constructible. Its finitely many nonzero cohomology sheaves have finite locally closed stratifications on which they are locally constant of finite type. Fix one such sheaf $G=H^qN$ and one of its strata $S$. The inverse-image calculation of Step 4 identifies $T(G)|_S$ with $\mathcal Hom_A(F|_S,G|_S)$. Take a joint etale covering on which these two inputs are constant with values $M$ finite projective and $B$ finitely generated. The finite-summand calculation gives the constant value $\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,B)$, a direct summand of $B^r$ and therefore finitely generated. This is precisely local constancy of finite type in [def-weil-pbc-locally-constant-finite-type-modules]. The same finite stratification [def-constructible-stratification] thus witnesses constructibility of $T(G)$. Step 5 identifies these sheaves with all the cohomology sheaves of the internal Hom, and Step 7 bounds their degrees. This proves the constructibility clause.

source.place: Lemma 7.6.11, first paragraph: preservation of constructibility

Sources checked: ILO XVII 7.2.1-7.2.7, 7.3.1-7.3.8, 7.6.4-7.6.11 (pp. 301-314) and 11.1.1/11.2.1. The item statement is identical to the version the Q57 reviewer landed. The coefficient category is ordinary etale A_X-modules with A a Noetherian F_l-algebra, as in ILO. The W_P class equals ILO FCons_P: sheaves constant on V_i are local systems by 7.2.4, extensions of torsion local systems are local systems by 7.2.5, and the class is closed under filtered colimits. Step 1: F[0] is K-flat with Tor amplitude [0,0], and the flat model with a=b=0 gives E^0 = F and a Galois partition Q with finite projective values. Step 2: the geometric point factors through its reduced stratum and lifts to the split finite etale fibre; comparing constant pullbacks gives that M is projective. Step 3: the Hom sheaf is the image of an idempotent, hence exact; cover detection applies, the evaluation node applies on each localized chart, and D is flat. Step 4: g^*D is constant on W_i, so D is in W_Q. Step 5: T(K) -> T(I) is a quasi-isomorphism and H^q = D tensor H^qN. Steps 6-7: the common refinement from exact-refinement plus the new node give the [u,v] bound, independent of N. Step 8: constructibility from Hom_A(M,B), a summand of B^r. New node: true by the pi_1 ind-unipotent description (11.2.1(i),(vii),(x),(xi)), using the tensor filtration and filtered colimits, with no flatness needed. It is strictly smaller than the item, not a restated clause, and genuinely needed. No duplicate found among the Galois-partition nodes (exact-refinement, finite-monodromy-filtration, flat-model). It meets B1-B9 and has all three search kinds. Correct blueprint from/via; same_as []. The item's from.place change to Step 3 is confirmed in the main-20261015 proof text. No SGA citation.
